title: Post-retraction citation: a case for radiology-imaging diagnostic
author: Sorana D. Bolboacă
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zcxf2xn
materials: Software Statistical analysis was conducted with Statistica program (StatSoft USA, v. 8). Microsoft Excel was used for graphicala representations.

steps.title: Define and Execute Search Strategy
steps.instruction: Perform a search in PubMed Clinical Queries using specific keywords and restrictions to identify retracted radiology-imaging diagnostic publications.

substeps.instruction: Use keywords: ((diagnostic or diagnosis) and (imaging or radiology)) AND ((Retracted Publication[sb] OR Retraction of Publication[sb]))
Apply restrictions: Clinical Study Categories Category = Diagnosis, Scope = Broad, Species = Humans, and Languages = English
Execute search on June 15, 2017, and store the links to all retrieved articles

steps.title: Collect Retracted Article Data
steps.instruction: Extract detailed metadata and characteristics for articles that meet the eligibility criteria based on publication year and month.

substeps.instruction: Collect: reported imaging diagnostic method, manuscript type (e.g., case report, case series, review, research article), journal name, number of authors, author affiliation, and country
Collect: month and year of retraction and the reason for retraction
Retrieve journal domain and rank from https://apps.webofknowledge.com/ where available
Calculate the time from publication to retraction in months

steps.title: Collect Citation Data
steps.instruction: Search the Scopus database in September 2017 using the titles of retracted articles to analyze citations before and after retraction.

substeps.instruction: Identify number of prior retraction citations and post-retraction citations based on the month/year of retraction and the month/year of the citing article's publication
Store links to articles citing retracted manuscripts (as of September 2017)
Filter citing articles for eligibility: full text available, language = English, and subject = humans

Between September and December 2017, collect for each citing article: title, journal name, year, number of authors, country of authors, type of citation (positive/negative), and whether it was identified in the text or reference as a retracted article
Record the reason for any post-retraction citation excluded from the analysis

steps.title: Categorize Data and Calculate Variables
steps.instruction: Split the dataset into groups and calculate specific citation indices and timeframes.

substeps.instruction: Split articles into two groups: ultrasound (US) diagnostic method vs. all other imaging diagnostic methods (non-US). If an article reports multiple methods and one is US, include it in the US group
Document characteristics of retracted articles: manuscript type, JCR journal rank (for WoS indexed journals), number of authors, and reason for retraction
Calculate time from publication to retraction (months)
Calculate time from citation to retraction (years)
Calculate Weighted Citation Index (WCI) as the ratio between number of citations and the citation time window (no. of months/12) for both prior (WCI prior) and post (WCI post) retraction
Create two dichotomial variables to determine if the number of post-retraction citations and WCI post were higher than those before retraction

steps.title: Perform Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the collected quantitative and categorical data using appropriate statistical tests.

substeps.instruction: Test normality of quantitative data using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
Compare US and non-US groups using the Mann Whitney test
Investigate the association between positive/negative post-retraction citations and diagnostic technique (US/non-US) using the Chi-square test

description: Title and abstract screening Where to look after the abstract? PubMed ( https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/) or on the journal page if no abstract was available in PubMed Inclusion criteria for diagnostic-related technique: radiography, radioscopy, ultrasonography (US, all types), computer tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography (PET), single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), or scintigraphy Reason for exclusion from the analysis
